title.narrative: Integrated Food Crisis Multi-Sector Emergency Response Consortium for the Food Security, Livelihoods, Health, Nutrition, and WASH support for IDPs and Hosts in Eddaein and Baher al Arab, East Darfur

description.narrative: ltpgtltbrgtAlight, in collaboration with CARE, AMVO, SADO, UPO, and GAH, is launching a comprehensive Food Security and Livelihoods (FSL) project that integrates critical nutrition, health, and Water, Sanitation, and Hygiene (WASH) interventions for internally displaced persons (IDPs) and resident communities in East Darfur Sudan. The consortium's mission is to address food security needs, deliver life-saving nutrition and health services, and ensure the well-being, reduced mortality, and morbidity of those affected by conflict. The FSL interventions include emergency agricultural support with a focus on crop protection, seed distribution, and livestock activities, alongside awareness sessions and capacity building for farmers. There will be in-kind support for seeds and local tools, distribution of post-harvest materials, and investments in livestock services, which are expected to benefit 359,315 individuals. In terms of health service intervention, the consortium plans to establish and operate Primary Health Care Centers (PHCCs) in the Eddaein locality and provide essential support to Baher Alarab Hospital. This support will encompass medical equipment, supplies, and furniture, as well as covering the costs associated with healthcare service providers and operational expenses. The primary healthcare package will include outpatient consultations, Expanded Program on Immunization (EPI) support, reproductive and maternal child health services, and facilitation of access to secondary healthcare for critical cases. Nutrition interventions will focus on Outpatient Therapeutic Programs (OTPs) and Targeted Supplementary Feeding Programs (TSFP), support referrals to Stabilization Centers (SC), conduct Mid-Upper Arm Circumference (MUAC) screening, and provide Infant and Young Child Nutrition (IYCN) counseling. These efforts will target IDPs, refugees, returnees, and host community members, especially those affected by food insecurity. WASH integration will contribute to safe, timely, and gender-responsive access to essential water and sanitation facilities. The consortium will provide 30,000 liters of water per month to 10 IDP gathering sites, ensuring a minimum of 8.5 liters per person per day, and distribute 500 standard family hygiene kits to households with severely acutely malnourished (SAM) children under five. Monitoring and accountability measures will be in place to support 36,000 people, including women, men, girls, and boys. All services will be provided free of charge to ensure equitable access. A multi-sectoral approach will be adopted to address cross-cutting issues and prevent and respond to Sexual Exploitation, Abuse, and Harassment (PSEAH) risks. This includes incorporating PSEAH awareness sessions into our interventions and empowering beneficiaries to report incidents safely and confidentially. Alight and its partners are committed to ensuring conflict sensitive programming and accountability to the affected population by maintaining transparency and responsiveness throughout the project cycle. This includes mitigation of risks associated with response and providing beneficiaries with access to project information through appropriate channels and languages and establishing mechanisms for collecting feedback and complaints. The consortium members will actively engage in emergency preparedness and response planning, bolstering resilience and preparedness within the communities we serve. In response to the urgent humanitarian need in Sudan, our consortium has proposed a 6-month project to deliver food security and livelihood interventions integrated with nutrition, health, and WASH life-saving assistance to conflict-affected and vulnerable populations in East Darfur state's Eldaein and Baher al Arab localities.ltbrgtlt/pgt
